_comment: Edge Case Evaluation Configuration - shared by Java and Python
_methodology_note: IMPORTANT: Edge cases were extracted from prediction errors of the 4 trained algorithms. Evaluating those same models on these edge cases is CIRCULAR - by construction, they already failed on these texts. Results should be interpreted as 'error characterization' (understanding WHY models fail) not 'robustness benchmarking' (measuring generalization). For valid robustness testing, use a held-out 5th algorithm or evaluate only on edge cases from OTHER domains.

edge_case_definition._comment: Defines what qualifies as an edge case vs a one-off model error
edge_case_definition.rationale: Threshold set to 4 (unanimous failure across all algorithms). Of 7,178 unique misclassified texts, 924 failed all 4 models vs 897 failing exactly 3. Unanimous failure provides the strongest signal of systematic difficulty rather than model-specific variance.

evaluation._min_samples_rationale: Categories with fewer samples are excluded from metrics (CI too wide to be meaningful). Currently excludes: sarcasm (n=2).

categories.name: Label Error
categories.description: Ground truth label is wrong (e.g., clearly positive review labeled negative)

categories.name: Sarcasm
categories.description: Surface sentiment contradicts true intent (e.g., 'Oh great, another broken product')

categories.name: Mixed Sentiment
categories.description: Contains both positive and negative aspects (e.g., 'Great features but terrible support')

categories.name: Negation Heavy
categories.description: Complex negation patterns (e.g., 'I can't say I didn't like it')

categories.name: Domain Jargon
categories.description: Domain-specific terms requiring context (e.g., 'sick beats' = positive in music)
